description: A school principal must finalize a temporary relocation plan for an early-childhood classroom during a boiler repair, including the classroom site, medication handling, student-support layout, and meal service, with input from facilities, the school nurse, a special education coordinator, and the cafeteria manager.

shared_context.S1: The boiler serving the early-childhood wing requires repair, and the classroom must operate elsewhere for ten school days beginning January 8.
shared_context.S2: The affected classroom serves 20 students and currently has its own tables, nap mats, and teaching materials.
shared_context.S3: The draft relocation plan places the class in Room B204, keeps medication handling under the regular classroom routine, uses the standard furniture arrangement, and serves lunch in the classroom.
shared_context.S4: Ms. Hart makes the final relocation decision and signs the operating plan.
shared_context.S5: The school's relocation procedure includes a routine check-in with facilities, the nurse, special education, and food service before the principal signs a temporary classroom plan.

PF1.text: Mr. Lewis's facilities inspection found that Room B204 cannot be used for an early-childhood class during the repair because its required egress door will be blocked by the repair staging. He confirmed the Library's clearance and available floor area with the custodian this morning, but the room-status board has not been updated.

PF2.text: Nurse Romero's health-plan review shows that one student needs refrigerated medication kept in the nurse's office, with a nurse check at exactly 10:00 a.m. each relocation day. She verified the plan with the student's family this week, but has not added the instruction to the classroom relocation draft.

PF3.text: Dr. Shah's classroom observation shows that one student requires a defined quiet area and a scheduled 15-minute quiet block after arrival each day. She confirmed the support with the student's case team yesterday, but the temporary-room layout has not been revised.

PF4.text: Ms. Greene's service review shows that the cafeteria can serve this class only at exactly 11:30 a.m. during the repair period; classroom meal delivery would leave the class without the required allergen-controlled service setup. She confirmed the capacity with the food-service scheduler this morning, but the draft still lists classroom lunch.

acceptance_conditions: The class must be relocated to the Library.
The Library's temporary-room clearance must be recorded.
Medication must be kept in the nurse's office.
A nurse check must occur at exactly 10:00 a.m.
A defined quiet area must be provided.
The daily quiet block must be exactly 15 minutes.
Lunch must be served in the cafeteria at exactly 11:30 a.m.
A cafeteria-service commitment must be recorded.
The facilities finding must be cited in the principal's justification.

decisive_facts.why: The facilities inspection changes the room from the draft's B204 to the Library and adds the required temporary-room clearance record.
The health-plan review changes medication storage to the nurse's office and sets the nurse check at exactly 10:00 a.m.
The case-team confirmation changes the room layout by requiring a defined quiet area and an exactly 15-minute daily quiet block.
The food-service review changes lunch from classroom delivery to the cafeteria at exactly 11:30 a.m. and requires a cafeteria-service commitment.
